prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1215; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant is represented by counsel, and the file has been opened for bodily injury and property damage.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the lane-change sideswipe as described in the first notice of loss.

Entry 4: Statements taken from two independent witnesses and the other driver. All three describe the collision the same way, and photos from the scene are consistent with that account.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage. The location and pattern of the damage match the described impact, and there is no sign of earlier damage to the vehicle in the records or on inspection.

Entry 6: Claimant's counsel provided the medical file. The reported neck and back strain fits the kind and force of the crash, and no prior treatment to the same body area appears in the records.

Entry 7: Follow-up interview with the claimant. Some small details were added to the account, but the core description of the collision has not changed from the first statement.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant improved. Provider notes show steady progress with no unusual gaps or escalation.

Entry 9: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start. Recommend proceeding with evaluation of the bodily injury and property damage claims under standard handling.
